evidence_meaning: Each accepted synthetic movement joins its typed request/result or actual commerce request, decision actor, and transaction timestamp.
Expense payment requires a prior approval; settlement requires a non-self reviewer; correction and count movements require their resolved review records.
A movement timestamp before its required decision does not satisfy the audit.
A saved log or attestation is not evidence that physical cash changed hands.
limits: PGlite is disposable PostgreSQL-compatible test infrastructure, not Render/Neon or a native-PostgreSQL production rehearsal.
Persisted actor IDs and confirmations prove the consistency of synthetic records, not the presence or intent of an actual human.
No claim is made about unknown legacy/production movements; this audit did not query them.
Transaction timestamps establish record ordering, not the time of a physical handover.
The new-cash-refund check is static source/config evidence; no real refund was attempted and no Prisma commerce runtime test was run in this task.
Full repository typecheck could not be completed after npm ci because Prisma generation attempted to reach the unavailable binaries.prisma.sh host; the executable test files passed through tsx.
